ops.title: ghapi: Paginate has no absolute page cap
ops.description:
Paginate (internal/ghapi/ghapi.go) gained cycle detection on 2026-08-01: it keys a `seen` set on the resolved target and fails before re-issuing a repeated rel="next" URL. That catches a server echoing the same link, but NOT a server minting a fresh unique rel="next" forever — the loop is still unbounded in that case, and reviews.go polls on a 30s cycle with no overall deadline, so `items` grows until OOM.

Deliberately left: the repeated-URL guard covers the realistic failure (buggy proxy, GHE quirk), and an absolute cap is a number nobody can justify from evidence today. Revisit if a real unbounded walk is ever observed, or if a caller appears that paginates an endpoint with genuinely unbounded pages.

ops.text: Either a justified page cap lands with the reasoning recorded, or the task is closed as no-fix with evidence
